precepts.text: The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel, his thoughts like a rolling axletree: three is one, one is three, in circles without end.
precepts.point: If a wise man contends with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh there is no rest: it is a circular argument that goes nowhere.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.why:
“If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man”: if a wise man debates with a stupid man or woman. And “whether he rage or laugh”: whether that fool laughs at it or is angry at it, “there is no rest.” There is no conclusion. It is a circular argument; you argue the same thing over and over again and it goes nowhere.

Sirach shows why: “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” The fool is a circular idiot. His mind just goes in circles, nonstop. That is the Trinity man: three is one, one is three, they are all the same, the Father and the Son of one substance. Round and round, and you cannot win. They are dead set in it, their minds sealed as with a hot iron.

Show them that the Father has sons, the children of Israel, and they cannot understand it: no, they are all one. Stump them in a debate and they keep going: but what about this? It is ongoing. It is a cartwheel. They will not yield to reason. Even the German had some sense when he called insanity doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

So leave that negro alone. You are wasting your time. These are unreasonable people, and you have to let them go. The wise man who keeps contending with the fool gets no rest, because the fool's heart only rolls in circles of nonsense.

precepts.text: Much knowledge the Lord hath divided them, and made their ways diverse. Some of them hath he blessed and exalted; some of them hath he sanctified and set near himself. But some of them hath he cursed and brought low: that's Esau. As the clay is in the potter's hand, to fashion it at his pleasure, so man is in the hand of him that made him.
precepts.point: Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour: that's Jacob. And another unto dishonour: that's Esau.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” Sirach shows the same potter at work: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth: In much knowledge the Lord hath divided them, and made their ways diverse.”

“Some of them hath he blessed and exalted and some of them he sanctified, and set near himself”: that is Jacob, whom he loved. “but some of them hath he cursed and brought low, and turned out of their places”: that is Esau, whom he hated. The vessels of wrath “fitted to destruction”, fitted meaning created, are Esau.

“As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.” Think of a movie: the writer has to have a good guy and a bad guy, and he hires you to be the bad guy. Why do I have to be the bad guy? Because I am paying you to be the bad guy. The pot cannot say to the one making it, why are you making me like this? It stays quiet, and the creator forms it and shapes it whichever way he will.

So it is “not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth”. You cannot will yourself to be the people of God; you cannot positively think your way into changing the mind of God, and you cannot run throughout the earth building churches to make yourself the people of God. The potter divided the lump, and the mercy goes to Jacob.

precepts.text: Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner. Look upon all the works of the most High, and there are two and two, one against another. There's always a good side and a bad side. You had a righteous Enoch and you had a wicked one.
precepts.point: And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” “So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.” There is always a good side and a bad side.

Genesis 5 shows it. “Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch.” Wait a minute: didn't Cain have a son named Enoch too? He did. Seth's Enoch “walked with God: and he was not; for God took him,” taken up the way Elijah was, walking with God just as Noah walked with God. You had a righteous Enoch and a wicked Enoch.

It goes on down the line. Seth's line had Methuselah, who lived “nine hundred sixty and nine years,” the longest of any man, and Lamech, who named his son Noah, “saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed,” the ground cursed when Adam sinned. Cain's line had its own Lamech. Two and two, one against another.

precepts.text: Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun? By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: some of them hath he made high days and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun?” “By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.” “Some of them hath he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.”

The same sun lights every day, but the Lord made some days high days and hallowed them. That is one man esteeming one day above another. What the Lord did back then to esteem the sabbath was two lambs a year old offered on that day.

Then Christ came and fulfilled that, and the Pharisees said, hell no; go back to that lamb, go back to that goat. That is what they were doing, judging the people in respect of the holyday, the new moon and the sabbath for not bringing the sacrifices that esteemed those days.

precepts.text: All men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth. The second witness.
precepts.point: The other nations make sure we are deficient in these things; a lot of the foods we eat diminish them. So it is important that we maintain a healthy diet, brothers and sisters.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

precepts.why:
Genesis 2:7 says “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” People talk about evolution, that man came up from primates and formed over time into what we know today; that is not true. Everything in Israel United in Christ is done to edify the nation, and what we say we prove out of the word of God. Ecclesiasticus 33:10 is the second witness: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.”

Some will ask how we know man was made from the dust, since that is not what the white man’s science says. Science is only good if it goes with the Bible; if it contradicts the Bible, we don't give a damn about science. But the honest science agrees. The infographic From Dust to Dust, the elements that connect us to Earth, shows that the human body is made mainly of elements also found in soil. The six main elements of life, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur, are in every cell, molecule and structure of the body and make up over 99 percent of our mass. The essential minerals, calcium for bones and teeth, potassium for the muscles and heart, magnesium, sodium and chlorine, are the same nutrients the soil gives the plants. The trace elements, iron for carrying oxygen, zinc for the immune system and healing, silicon and manganese, are in the soil too. We come from the earth, and to the earth we return, just like the Bible says.

The Most High is a mastermind, the author of beauty, the creator of all things, and he knew what he was doing when he pulled Adam from the dust of the ground. Our bodies are a testament that his word is true. The Bible is a true book, and we don't give a damn what anybody has to say about how our God, our father, created us. The teaching that man came from primates is there to contradict God’s word, because they know our God is a black man.

Paul says the same: “The first man is of the earth, earthy,” and “As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy.” Adam was earthy, and so are we; we come from the same soil as our father Adam, and “as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.” Meanwhile the other nations make sure we are deficient in these very things, and much of the food we eat diminishes them to kill us faster. So it is important, brothers and sisters, to keep a healthy diet.

precepts.text: Send him to labour that he be not idle, for idleness teacheth much evil.
precepts.point: They that consent unto them shall be had in derision and trodden under foot: nobody likes a traitor, and like the donkeys in Planet of the Apes, Esau uses you and gets rid of you. In every place and in the next cities a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord, which is why Christ said flee to the next city.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. That great multitude is what Christ said: you shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And “they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle”. Idle, i-d-l-e: a person avoiding work; lazy, indolent, slothful, workshy, shiftless, loafing; without purpose or effect, pointless.

In this truth, if you are idle you are avoiding work. Not work in the world: God's work. You are lazy in this truth. You have no purpose; you are just here. Some of you have been here for years and you have no office, doing nothing. You are idle.

“Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.” Brothers and sisters, when you are idle in the truth, you are learning evil. That is why you spend your time on porn, smoking cigarettes, smoking weed, hitting women up in their DMs. You have idle time, and there is a whole lot of work in this truth to be done.

We can spot that idleness as soon as you come in: the one who sits down and just looks around, looking at the women's side, taking no notes. If this means something to you, you are engulfed in it; you are writing things down and trying to put it to memory. The idle are the certain ones the multitude will take away and feed.

precepts.text: Consider that I labor not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning. Captains left at 4 a.m. to teach and check the congregation; bishops and deacons travel the world. Be nation-minded, not me, me, me.
precepts.point: Because he asked understanding and not long life, riches, or the life of his enemies, God gave him a wise and understanding heart like none before or after. When your mind is for the people, the Lord blesses beyond measure and gives more than you desired.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Solomon’s mind was on the people. He did not ask for four hundred women or chariots, or to be a king of 4,000; he asked for “an understanding heart to judge thy people”, “for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?” Because he had a mind for the people, the Lord elevated him and gave him more than he even desired for himself. Likewise with us: when we have a mind for the people, the Lord will bless that thing beyond measure.

Sirach says it plainly: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” In this truth we are not doing this for ourselves. Captains left at four in the morning, driving, so they could be here to help teach the class. A captain drove down and got here at five in the morning to check the congregation, to check on the saints of the Most High. The bishops travel all over the world; the deacons travel. This is not for ourselves; this is for the nation of Israel, because we understand the kingdom that is at hand.

“but for all them”: this is a nation. You must be nation-minded. A lot of times we are not like that: me, me, me, me, me, and that is all you are concerned with. But all through the Bible the greatest leaders were focused on the nation of Israel and how to move the nation further ahead.

That is the mindset of a leader and the action of a king: like Solomon, labour not for yourself only, but for all the people, and the Lord gives more than you asked.

precepts.text: A man of understanding trusteth in the law, and the law is faithful unto him. Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard: in prayer, in the streets, in leading and organizing blacks and Hispanics. Bind up instruction, and then make answer.
precepts.point: Ezra had prepared his heart, his mind, to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments. We are in captivity, working and tired, and the Most High reminds us these are the last days, so prepare your mind.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law and to teach it. Sirach shows why: “A man of understanding trusteth in the law; and the law is faithful unto him, as an oracle.” We must trust in the laws of God, and the law will be faithful unto us.

“Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard”. We have to prepare what to say. Prepare what to say in prayer when we speak to the Most High, and we will be heard. Prepare what to say and teach in the streets, and we will be heard. We must prepare to lead, guide and organize blacks and Hispanics.

“and bind up instruction, and then make answer.” Bind up the instruction first, and then make answer. That is how Ezra could teach in Israel statutes and judgments: he had prepared his heart before he opened his mouth.

precepts.text: Be not excessive toward any, and without discretion do nothing. Ask why you are eating: nourishment, or because it looks, smells, tastes, and sounds good five minutes after you ate? A nymphomaniac wants sex all the time, but sex was created for procreation and beyond that becomes pleasure, and there is no level of pleasure at which the flesh is finally fulfilled. What high are you looking for when you smoke weed, since you always come down? There is only fulfillment in disciplining your spirit and keeping the commandments.
precepts.point: Whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things: when am I going to eat, the things pleasing to the eyes and the flesh. Overindulging outside God's guidelines takes you out of the realm of discipline into the realm of Satan.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“Be not excessive toward any; and without discretion do nothing.” Do not be excessive toward anything. You might say, but I am hungry. Then ask yourself why you are eating. Is it for nourishment, the proper nutrients? Or because it looks good, smells good, tastes good, because you like the sound of it? Are outside things programming you, catering to the lust of the flesh through your eyes and your ears? Did you eat just five minutes ago and now you have to get a snack?

Some are excessive even with sex, a nymphomaniac, wanting sex all the time. Sex was created for procreation; outside of that it becomes pleasure. How much pleasure until the body is completely fulfilled? There is never an end to it. The same with weed: what high are you looking for, when you always come down? There is no fulfillment in smoking weed, drinking alcohol, the excess of sex, or overeating.

That is why the scriptures speak of the holy spirit of discipline. The only fulfillment is in disciplining your spirit and keeping God’s commandments. Once you go outside the realm of discipline, you are catering to the realm of Satan, and you open yourself to be a target and to be controlled at any level. That is the mind of those who “mind earthly things” in Philippians 3.

precepts.point: The idle in the truth will be fed Christianity. Those two years or more in the congregation must examine themselves.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
The great multitude “shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” Spell that word: i-d-l-e. “Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.”

Idle means a person avoiding work: lazy, indolent, slothful, shiftless, inactive, sluggish, lethargic; without purpose or effect. Those words fit some of you in here, men and women. Not the new people who just came, but those who have been with us two years or more. What are you doing? Do you have an office? Is there something you are doing here in Israel? If not, you are idle, and idleness teaches much evil.

And what will the idle be fed? Things offered unto idols, i-d-o-l: an image or representation of a god used as an object of worship. Look at the images of the Roman Catholic Church; those are idols. One word: Christianity.

So the ones the multitude takes away and feeds with idolatry are the ones with no purpose in here. Because you were idle, you will be seduced and given Christianity, that idolatrous religion. Stay busy in the work of the Most High.

precepts.point: The whole scripture is good set against evil: the godly against the sinner, Jacob against Esau, righteousness against sin. Two powerful forces were being born into the earth, and the struggle began in the womb.

note.label: Genesis 25: Two Nations in the Womb

precepts.why:
“The children struggled together within her.” That struggle is the whole scripture in a womb: “Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly. So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.”

Jacob against Esau, the godly against the sinner, righteousness against sin. Two nations, two manner of people, one stronger than the other, and the elder to serve the younger. Two powerful forces were being born into the earth, and the struggle began in the womb.

precepts.text: Every day has the same sun, but by the knowledge of the Lord some days were made high days and hallowed; the sabbath is distinguished by God, not by man.
precepts.point: Six days may work be done, but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD. It is more than a day of rest and congregating; it is the sign of who Israel's God is, which is why saying the sabbath is done away takes away the very sign between Israel and God.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun? By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts. Some of them hath he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.”

Every day has the same sun, but the sabbath is distinguished by God, not by man. “Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep: for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations”. Keeping the weekly sabbath and the feast days shows that Israel are his children and he is their God. The nations do not have this sabbath; adopted Sunday worship is not the true sabbath given to the children of Israel, for it was not hallowed by the knowledge of the Lord.

precepts.text: One day excels another by the knowledge of the Lord: some days He made high days and hallowed them, and some He made ordinary.
precepts.point: It is a holy convocation, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.” The Most High gave us holy days, and He Himself proclaimed them. “Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun? By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.”

“Some of them hath he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.” The Passover, Tabernacles, the new moon and the Sabbath are the high days He made; the days He did not name are ordinary days.

So a holiday not listed in this Bible and not ordained of the Most High has nothing holy about it. Only His knowledge distinguishes one day from another.

precepts.text: Good is set against evil and the godly against the sinner; God's laws are contrary to sin.
precepts.point: He preserveth the souls of His saints and delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” God's laws are contrary to sin; the two stand one against the other. “So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.”

That is why loving the Lord and hating evil go together. If you love his commandments, you are set against sin, the godly against the sinner.

precepts.text: We were brought down to the serving class because of sin.
precepts.point: Bread, correction, and work are for a servant. We have been brought down to the serving class because of sin, because of disobedience to God's commandments.

note.label: Proverbs 19: Discipline, the Fear of the Lord, and Servitude

precepts.why:
“Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.” The Most High is preparing us for the kingdom, and he will beat that foolishness out of us.

Ecclesiasticus tells what is set aside for whom: “Fodder, a wand, and burdens, are for the ass; and bread, correction, and work, for a servant.” Bread, correction and work are for a servant. That is where we are: we have been brought down to the serving class because of sin, because of disobedience to God's commandments.

So the stripes for the back of fools are not random. Correction belongs to the servant, and Israel is in the servant's place until the foolishness is beaten out and we are ready for the kingdom.

precepts.text: Correction and work are appointed for a servant, matching the rod for the fool's back.
precepts.point: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back. Ecclesiasticus says the same: correction and work are for a servant, and that correction is the rod for the fool's back.

note.label: Proverbs 26: Honor Is Not Fitting for a Fool

precepts.why:
“A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool’s back.” Each one has what is fitted to it, and what fits the fool is the rod.

Ecclesiasticus says the same: “Fodder, a wand, and burdens, are for the ass; and bread, correction, and work, for a servant.” Correction and work are appointed for a servant, and that correction is the rod for the fool's back. The ass gets the wand and the burdens; the servant gets bread, correction and work.

That is why honor is not seemly for a fool, like snow in summer and rain in harvest. What is fitted to him is not honor but the rod.
